faq.title: Everything you're wondering about a zero-fee marketplace

free.q: Is Freelancezero really free — what's the catch?
free.a: Yes. Freelancezero charges freelancers and clients 0% — no commissions, no connects, no withdrawal fees. There is no catch: the platform is a coordinator, not a middleman that skims payments. We sustain the project through optional premium tools and services that never gate the core marketplace.

difference.q: How is Freelancezero different from Upwork?
difference.a: The biggest difference is fees: Upwork takes up to 10% of your earnings, plus paid “connects” to apply and payment-processing markups. Freelancezero takes nothing. You also choose your own payout processor (Stripe, PayPal, Wise, or crypto), own and export your data anytime, and get faster, AI-assisted matching.

payment.q: How do freelancers get paid if the platform takes no fee?
payment.a: Payments flow directly from client to freelancer through a processor you choose. Freelancezero coordinates milestones and releases but never holds your money, so there's no platform cut and often faster access to funds.

import.q: Can I import my Upwork profile and reviews?
import.a: Yes. Our import tool helps you rebuild your profile — bio, skills, portfolio, and work history — in minutes so switching doesn't mean starting from zero.

safety.q: Is it safe? How are disputes handled?
safety.a: Clients can be payment- and identity-verified, reviews are transparent and double-blind to prevent retaliation, and disputes use a fast, transparent, community-led resolution process with optional arbitration.

agencies.q: Do you support agencies and teams?
agencies.a: Yes. Agencies can add team members with roles, manage a shared pipeline, and bid or deliver as a team — with the same zero-fee model.

meta.title: Privacy Policy
meta.description: How Freelancezero collects, uses, and protects your personal data. We never sell your data, and you can export or delete it at any time.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: We collect the minimum we need to run the marketplace, we never sell your data, and you can take it with you or delete it at any time.

whoWeAre.title: Who we are
whoWeAre.body: Freelancezero (“we”, “us”) operates a zero-fee freelance marketplace. This policy explains what we do with personal data when you use the hosted service at freelancezero.com. Freelancezero is also open source and self-hostable — if you are using someone else's instance, that operator is the data controller, not us.

whatWeCollect.title: What we collect
items: Account data: name, email address, password hash, and profile photo if you upload one.
Profile data: headline, bio, skills, rates, portfolio items, and work history you choose to publish.
Marketplace activity: job postings, proposals, messages, contracts, and reviews.
Payout preferences: the payment method you select and a display-only identifier (for example a PayPal email). We never take custody of funds and we do not store full bank credentials.

Technical data: audit-log entries for security-sensitive actions such as sign-in and payout changes. Audit logs are deliberately minimal — we do not store IP addresses or browser user agents alongside them.

howWeUse.title: How we use it
items: To operate the marketplace: matching freelancers with jobs, delivering proposals, and enabling messaging.
To send transactional email: email confirmation, sign-in links, application notifications, and security alerts.
To keep the platform safe: preventing spam, fraud, and abuse, and reviewing accounts before approval.
To meet legal obligations and resolve disputes.

privacy.howWeUseNote: We do not sell your personal data, and we do not use it to train advertising profiles.

legalBases.title: Legal bases (GDPR)
legalBases.body: Where the GDPR applies, we process personal data under: performance of a contract (running your account and the marketplace), legitimate interests (security, fraud prevention, product improvement), consent (optional communications, which you can withdraw), and legal obligation (tax and compliance records).

sharing.title: Sharing
sharing.body: We share data only with processors that make the service work — our hosting provider, our database host, and our transactional email provider. They act on our instructions and are bound by contract. When you apply to a job, your name, profile, and proposal are shared with that client; that is the point of the platform.

retention.title: Retention
retention.body: We keep account data while your account is open. When you delete your account we begin a grace period, after which personal data is erased or irreversibly anonymised. Records we are legally required to keep (for example, transaction ledgers) are retained for the statutory period.

yourRights.title: Your rights
items: Access and export: download your data, including your profile and portfolio.
Rectification: correct anything inaccurate from your settings page.
Erasure: delete your account and associated personal data.
Objection and restriction: ask us to stop specific processing.
Complaint: raise a concern with your local data protection authority.

privacy.yourRightsNote: To exercise any of these, email privacy@freelancezero.com.

cookies.title: Cookies
cookies.body: We use strictly necessary cookies for authentication and security. We do not use advertising or cross-site tracking cookies.

changes.title: Changes
changes.body: If we make material changes we will update the date above and, where the change is significant, notify you by email. Questions? See our <termsLink>Terms</termsLink> and <securityLink>Security</securityLink> pages.

terms.title: Terms of Service
terms.intro: The rules for using Freelancezero. We have tried to keep them short and readable, because terms nobody reads protect nobody.

agreement.title: 1. Agreement
agreement.body: By creating an account or using Freelancezero you agree to these Terms. If you are using the platform on behalf of a company, you confirm you are authorised to bind that company. If you do not agree, do not use the service.

whatIs.title: 2. What Freelancezero is — and is not
whatIs.body: Freelancezero is a venue that connects clients and freelancers. We charge no commission on your work. We are not a party to any contract you form with another user, we are not an employer or employment agency, and we do not supervise or guarantee any work performed.
whatIs.nonCustodial: Freelancezero is non-custodial: we never hold your money. Payments are arranged directly between client and freelancer using the method they choose.

eligibility.title: 3. Eligibility and accounts
items: You must be at least 18 years old and legally able to enter contracts.
You must provide accurate information and keep your profile current.
You are responsible for your account credentials and everything done under your account.
New accounts are reviewed before approval; we may decline or revoke approval at our discretion.
One person or organisation, one account, unless we agree otherwise in writing.

acceptableUse.title: 4. Acceptable use
items: Post false, misleading, discriminatory, or unlawful content, including fake jobs or fake reviews.
Harass, threaten, defraud, or impersonate anyone.
Scrape, overload, probe, or attempt to circumvent security controls on the platform.
Use the platform to send unsolicited bulk messages or spam.
Infringe anyone's intellectual property or confidentiality obligations.
acceptableUse.outro: We may suspend or terminate accounts that break these rules.

contracts.title: 5. Contracts between users
contracts.body: When a client accepts a proposal, the contract is between those two users. They decide scope, deliverables, timelines, payment terms, and IP ownership. We recommend agreeing these in writing before work starts. Any dispute is primarily between the parties; our optional dispute process is a good-faith facilitation, not binding arbitration, unless the parties separately agree to it.

payments.title: 6. Payments, taxes, and fees
payments.body: Freelancezero takes 0% of what you earn. Third-party payment providers you choose (for example Stripe, PayPal, or Wise) may charge their own processing fees, which are outside our control. You are solely responsible for determining, reporting, and paying your own taxes.

content.title: 7. Your content
content.body: You keep ownership of everything you post. You grant us a non-exclusive, worldwide, royalty-free licence to host, display, and distribute that content solely to operate and promote the service. You are responsible for having the rights to what you publish.

disclaimers.title: 8. Disclaimers
disclaimers.body: The service is provided “as is” and “as available”, without warranties of any kind to the fullest extent permitted by law. We do not warrant that the platform will be uninterrupted or error-free, or that any user is qualified, reliable, or will perform as promised. Vet your counterparties.

liability.title: 9. Limitation of liability
liability.body: To the maximum extent permitted by law, Freelancezero is not liable for indirect, incidental, special, consequential, or punitive damages, or for lost profits, revenue, data, or goodwill. Because we charge you nothing, our aggregate liability to you is limited to the greater of amounts you paid us in the prior twelve months (typically zero) or USD 100.

termination.title: 10. Termination
termination.body: You may close your account at any time. We may suspend or terminate access for breach of these Terms, legal requirements, or risk to the platform or its users. Provisions that by their nature should survive termination will survive.

openSource.title: 11. Open source
openSource.body: The Freelancezero software is released under the MIT licence. These Terms govern the hosted service at freelancezero.com; the software licence governs the code. Self-hosted instances are operated by whoever runs them, and we are not responsible for them.

changes.title: 12. Changes and contact

meta.title: Security
meta.description: How Freelancezero protects your account and data: encryption in transit, hashed passwords, non-custodial payments, and a public vulnerability disclosure process.

security.title: Security
security.intro: Freelancezero is open source, which means our security posture is auditable by anyone. Here is how we protect accounts and data — and how to report a problem.

account.title: Account security
items: Passwords are hashed with bcrypt (cost factor 12). We never store them in plain text and cannot read them.
Sign in with a password, a one-time email magic link, or Google/GitHub — whichever you prefer.

Two-factor authentication (TOTP) is on the roadmap. Today, accounts are protected by mandatory email confirmation, rate-limited authentication endpoints, and short-lived one-click recruiter links that are stored only as hashes.
Password accounts stay inert until the email address is confirmed — unverified accounts cannot sign in.
Security-sensitive changes, such as updating your payout method, trigger a notification email so you notice anything you did not do.

data.title: Data protection
items: All traffic is served over HTTPS/TLS.
Access to production data is restricted and audited; sensitive actions are written to an append-only audit log.
Uploaded files are validated by type and size and served from a path-traversal-safe route.
We collect the minimum personal data needed to run the marketplace — see our Privacy Policy.

payments.title: Payments are non-custodial
payments.body: Freelancezero never holds your money and never takes a commission. Funds move directly between client and freelancer through the provider they choose. We store a display-only identifier for your chosen payout method (for example a PayPal email) — never full banking credentials or card numbers. That means there is no pot of user funds on our side to steal.

safety.title: Marketplace safety
items: New accounts are manually reviewed before they can post jobs or apply.
Proposals carry a transparent quality score to keep low-effort spam out of client inboxes.
Outbound email honours one-click unsubscribe and suppression, so we do not become a spam vector.
Reviews are released double-blind to prevent retaliation bias.

disclosure.title: Responsible disclosure
disclosure.body: If you believe you have found a vulnerability, email security@freelancezero.com with steps to reproduce. Please give us a reasonable window to fix the issue before publishing, and avoid accessing other people's data, degrading the service, or running automated scans against production while testing.
disclosure.outro: We aim to acknowledge reports within three business days and will keep you updated on the fix. We are happy to credit researchers who report responsibly.

selfHosting.title: Self-hosting
selfHosting.body: Running your own instance? You own its security. At minimum: set a strong AUTH_SECRET, terminate TLS, keep the database off the public internet, apply updates promptly, and configure a verified sending domain with SPF, DKIM, and DMARC before enabling email.
